Usage: drive open <label> [<line> ...] [flags]

Open a new Claude Code session in Rex, in the batch, with an optional first step.

The session opens in a new Rex block in the batch's Rex session and joins
the batch under LABEL; the step, if given, is its first.

Arguments:
  <label>               The label the new session gets in the batch.
  <line> ...            The step as one line, typed as is, a slash command too; with --snippet, the
                        text the owner would type after the key (optional).

Flags:
      --file=PATH       Send this file instead: your own request, or anything longer than a line.
      --snippet=KEY     Send the owner's TabType snippet KEY, as it resolves in the session's
                        directory.
      --dir=DIR         The directory the session starts in (default: .).
      --resume=ID       Resume this Claude Code session id instead of starting fresh, such as a
                        session relaunched on another account.
      --account=NAME    Run it on this Claude account instead of the launcher's choice.
      --model=MODEL     Run it on this model, such as fable for a fresh judge.
      --hold=NAME       Name what its first turn uses that only one session may use at a time, as
                        send's --hold does.

Inherited flags:
  -h, --help            Show context-sensitive help.
      --batch=NAME      Act in this batch instead of the current one, which stays current. It may
                        stand anywhere on the line.

Constraints:
  At most one of --file, --snippet.

Steps:
  A step is one of:
    'one short line'        typed as is, a slash command too ('/write-spec Go with D1')
    --file PATH             sent as "Read <copy> and do what it asks."; drive keeps the copy
    --snippet KEY 'TEXT'    the owner's snippet for the session's directory, with the
                            step's words, TEXT, where the owner would type after it
  Text that starts with a dash goes after --, which ends the flags.
  The first step a session gets in a batch carries the owner's notice ahead of it.

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    refused: nothing was done; next: says what to run instead
  2    invalid arguments; nothing was run
  3    tried and did not end as asked; the message says what did happen
  4    the session's login was rejected; next: relaunches it on another account, or says to tell the
       owner
